$ agent-archive recover PREVIOUS_ID
\e[1mTranscript recovery\e[0m

Session PREVIOUS_ID cannot prove that the current transcript extends its
retained history.

\e[1mConsequences\e[0m

Recovery preserves its archived history, feedback and handoffs under
PREVIOUS_ID, freezes further native capture there, and starts a new linked
archive ID from the current filtered transcript. Missing earlier records remain a capture gap.
Each generation expires independently under normal retention. Existing subagents keep their original
identities and parent; new subagents use the active generation. Imported generations remain in their
original undo batch.
The new generation is queued locally for normal sync. Recovery permanently requires a
generation-aware writer; older binaries will refuse this data directory.

To start this generation, run agent-archive recover PREVIOUS_ID --confirm.
[exit 0]
$ agent-archive recover PREVIOUS_ID --confirm
\e[1mTranscript recovery\e[0m

Session PREVIOUS_ID cannot prove that the current transcript extends its
retained history.

\e[1mConsequences\e[0m

Recovery preserves its archived history, feedback and handoffs under
PREVIOUS_ID, freezes further native capture there, and starts a new linked
archive ID from the current filtered transcript. Missing earlier records remain a capture gap.
Each generation expires independently under normal retention. Existing subagents keep their original
identities and parent; new subagents use the active generation. Imported generations remain in their
original undo batch.
The new generation is queued locally for normal sync. Recovery permanently requires a
generation-aware writer; older binaries will refuse this data directory.

Queued new generation MACHINE_ID, linked to PREVIOUS_ID. Future hooks route to the new ID. Run agent-archive sync to publish it.
[exit 0]
